Clue 1: According to the ancient Protoevangelium of James, this saint's offering at the Temple was rejected because he had no children.
Clue 2: Tradition says he went into the wilderness to fast and pray for forty days, asking God for a child.
Clue 3: Tradition says an angel told him that his prayers had been answered.
Clue 4: His name is not found anywhere in the Bible; it comes from early Christian tradition.
Clue 5: He is a patron saint of fathers and grandfathers.
Clue 6: He shares his feast day, July 26, with his wife.
Clue 7: He and his wife were already old when their only child was born.
Clue 8: He is the grandfather of Jesus.
Clue 9: His wife is St. Anne.
Clue 10: He is the father of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

Clue 1: In the Protoevangelium of James, this saint wept over her childlessness under a laurel tree after seeing a nest of baby sparrows.
Clue 2: A famous basilica shrine near Quebec City, Canada, is dedicated to her and is known for healings.
Clue 3: Her name comes from the Hebrew word for "grace."
Clue 4: She is a patron saint of grandmothers and of women in labor.
Clue 5: She shares her feast day, July 26, with her husband.
Clue 6: She is often shown in art teaching her young daughter to read.
Clue 7: She and her husband were already old when their only child was born.
Clue 8: She is the grandmother of Jesus.
Clue 9: Her husband was St. Joachim.
Clue 10: She is the mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

Clue 1: Pope Pius IX declared this saint Patron of the Universal Church in 1870.
Clue 2: Pope Francis dedicated a special year to him from December 2020 to December 2021.
Clue 3: He is the patron saint of a happy death, because tradition says he died with Jesus and Mary at his side.
Clue 4: Many people bury a small statue of him in their yard when trying to sell a house.
Clue 5: He has two feast days: March 19, and May 1 as "the Worker."
Clue 6: An angel spoke to him in dreams, including one telling him to flee to Egypt.
Clue 7: He is the patron saint of workers and fathers.
Clue 8: He was a carpenter in Nazareth.
Clue 9: He was the husband of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
Clue 10: He was the foster father of Jesus.
Accepted Names: Joseph of Nazareth;Joseph the Worker;Joseph the Carpenter

Clue 1: This saint's father was a priest in the Temple who was struck mute for doubting an angel's message.
Clue 2: His mother Elizabeth was a relative of the Virgin Mary.
Clue 3: He leaped for joy in his mother's womb when the pregnant Virgin Mary came to visit.
Clue 4: His birthday, June 24, is one of only three birthdays on the Church calendar, along with those of Jesus and Mary.
Clue 5: He was beheaded at the request of the daughter of Herodias.
Clue 6: He wore clothing of camel's hair and ate locusts and wild honey.
Clue 7: He preached repentance in the wilderness near the Jordan River.
Clue 8: He pointed to Jesus and said, "Behold, the Lamb of God."
Clue 9: He was a cousin of Jesus.
Clue 10: He baptized Jesus in the Jordan River.

Clue 1: Early writers say this saint was thrown from the pinnacle of the Temple and then struck dead with a fuller's club.
Clue 2: Because of his martyrdom, he is often shown in art holding a club.
Clue 3: He is honored as the first bishop of Jerusalem.
Clue 4: He was known as "the Just" because of his holiness.
Clue 5: The New Testament letter that says "faith without works is dead" is traditionally credited to him.
Clue 6: He spoke at the Council of Jerusalem about welcoming Gentile believers.
Clue 7: He shares his feast day, May 3, with the Apostle Philip.
Clue 8: He was the son of Alphaeus.
Clue 9: He was one of two Apostles who shared the same first name.
Clue 10: He was called "the Less" or "the Younger" to tell him apart from James the Greater.
Accepted Names: James the Lesser;James the Minor;James son of Alphaeus

Clue 1: According to tradition, this saint was presented in the Temple as a little child, a feast kept on November 21.
Clue 2: Her birthday is celebrated on September 8.
Clue 3: In 1950, Pope Pius XII declared that she was taken body and soul into heaven.
Clue 4: She was conceived without original sin.
Clue 5: She is the patroness of the United States under the title of the Immaculate Conception.
Clue 6: She appeared to children at Lourdes and Fatima.
Clue 7: The Rosary is a prayer especially devoted to her.
Clue 8: The angel Gabriel greeted her with the words "Hail, full of grace."
Clue 9: She was the wife of St. Joseph.
Clue 10: She is the Mother of Jesus and the Mother of God.
Accepted Names: Mary;Virgin Mary;Blessed Virgin;Blessed Mother;Our Lady;Mother of God;Mother Mary;Madonna;Mary Mother of Jesus
Invocation: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for me!

Clue 1: According to tradition, this saint was martyred at Patras, in Greece.
Clue 2: He is the patron saint of Scotland, and his cross appears on the Scottish flag.
Clue 3: Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross.
Clue 4: His feast day, November 30, falls near the beginning of Advent.
Clue 5: He told Jesus about a boy who had five barley loaves and two fish.
Clue 6: He was a fisherman from Bethsaida in Galilee.
Clue 7: He was a disciple of John the Baptist before he followed Jesus.
Clue 8: He is called "the First-Called" because he was the first Apostle to follow Jesus.
Clue 9: He was one of the Twelve Apostles.
Clue 10: He was the brother of St. Peter.

Clue 1: According to tradition, this saint was fleeing Rome when he met the risen Lord and asked, "Quo vadis?" (Where are you going?)
Clue 2: Tradition says he was crucified upside down because he felt unworthy to die the same way as Jesus.
Clue 3: His tomb lies beneath the high altar of the great basilica in Vatican City.
Clue 4: He wrote two letters in the New Testament.
Clue 5: He is usually shown in art holding a set of keys.
Clue 6: He walked on water toward Jesus, then became afraid and began to sink.
Clue 7: He denied knowing Jesus three times before the rooster crowed.
Clue 8: His name was originally Simon, and he was a fisherman.
Clue 9: Jesus told him, "You are Rock, and upon this rock I will build my Church."
Clue 10: He was the first Pope.

Clue 1: According to legend, the Virgin Mary appeared to this saint on a pillar at Zaragoza, Spain, while she was still alive.
Clue 2: King Herod Agrippa had him killed with the sword, making him the first of the Twelve to die a martyr.
Clue 3: He is the patron saint of Spain.
Clue 4: A scallop shell is his symbol.
Clue 5: Pilgrims walk the Camino de Santiago to his shrine in northwest Spain.
Clue 6: Jesus called him and his brother "Boanerges," meaning "Sons of Thunder."
Clue 7: He was with Jesus at the Transfiguration and in the Garden of Gethsemane.
Clue 8: His father Zebedee was a fisherman.
Clue 9: He was one of two Apostles who shared the same first name, and he is called "the Greater."
Clue 10: He was the brother of St. John the Apostle.
Accepted Names: James the Great;James the Major;James son of Zebedee;Santiago

Clue 1: This saint was shipwrecked on the island of Malta and was unharmed by a snakebite there.
Clue 2: He was born in Tarsus, in what is now Turkey.
Clue 3: He made tents for a living.
Clue 4: He studied under the famous Jewish teacher Gamaliel.
Clue 5: Because he was a Roman citizen, he was beheaded in Rome rather than crucified.
Clue 6: He watched over the cloaks of the men who stoned St. Stephen.
Clue 7: He wrote the famous words "Love is patient, love is kind."
Clue 8: Before his conversion he was called Saul and persecuted Christians.
Clue 9: He was struck blind by a bright light on the road to Damascus.
Clue 10: He was the Apostle to the Gentiles and wrote much of the New Testament.
Accepted Names: Paul the Apostle;Paul of Tarsus;Saul;Saul of Tarsus

Clue 1: This saint was the first one named among the seven men chosen in the Acts of the Apostles to serve the widows in Jerusalem.
Clue 2: He gave a long speech before the Sanhedrin retelling the history of Israel.
Clue 3: Before he died, he saw the heavens open and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Clue 4: His feast day is December 26, the day after Christmas.
Clue 5: The Christmas carol "Good King Wenceslas" mentions his feast day.
Clue 6: Like Jesus, he prayed for the people who were killing him.
Clue 7: Saul, who later became St. Paul, approved of his death.
Clue 8: He was one of the first deacons of the Church.
Clue 9: He was stoned to death outside Jerusalem.
Clue 10: He was the first Christian martyr.
Accepted Names: Stephen the Protomartyr;Stephen the First Martyr

Clue 1: According to tradition, Venetian merchants smuggled this saint's body out of Alexandria hidden under pork.
Clue 2: He is the patron saint of Venice, where a famous basilica holds his relics.
Clue 3: He is honored as the founder of the Church in Alexandria, Egypt.
Clue 4: St. Peter called him "my son."
Clue 5: He set out with Paul and Barnabas on a missionary journey but left partway through.
Clue 6: His symbol is a winged lion.
Clue 7: Some think he was the young man who ran away without his clothes when Jesus was arrested.
Clue 8: His Gospel is the shortest of the four.
Clue 9: His Gospel is widely believed to be the first one written.
Clue 10: He wrote the second Gospel of the New Testament.

Clue 1: According to tradition, this saint was thrown into a cauldron of boiling oil in Rome and came out unharmed.
Clue 2: Tradition says he was the only one of the Twelve Apostles who did not die a martyr.
Clue 3: He was exiled to the island of Patmos.
Clue 4: Tradition says he wrote the Book of Revelation.
Clue 5: His symbol is an eagle.
Clue 6: His Gospel begins, "In the beginning was the Word."
Clue 7: He was the son of Zebedee and the brother of St. James the Greater.
Clue 8: He was the only Apostle standing at the foot of the Cross.
Clue 9: Jesus entrusted His mother Mary to his care.
Clue 10: He is called "the beloved disciple."
Accepted Names: John the Apostle;John the Evangelist;John the Beloved;Beloved Disciple

Clue 1: In 2016, Pope Francis raised this saint's July 22 memorial to the rank of a feast.
Clue 2: She is called "the Apostle to the Apostles."
Clue 3: Legend says she spent her last years praying in a cave in southern France.
Clue 4: Jesus cast seven demons out of her.
Clue 5: Her name comes from her hometown, a fishing village on the Sea of Galilee.
Clue 6: She was one of the women who supported Jesus and stood near the Cross.
Clue 7: She went to the tomb early on Easter morning.
Clue 8: At first she thought the risen Jesus was the gardener.
Clue 9: She recognized Jesus when He called her by name.
Clue 10: She was the first witness of the Resurrection.

Clue 1: This Apostle said to Jesus, "Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us."
Clue 2: Some Greeks came to him and said, "Sir, we would like to see Jesus."
Clue 3: Jesus tested him by asking where they could buy bread to feed a huge crowd.
Clue 4: He answered that two hundred days' wages would not buy enough bread for everyone.
Clue 5: Tradition says he was martyred at Hierapolis, in modern Turkey.
Clue 6: He shares his feast day, May 3, with St. James the Less.
Clue 7: Like Peter and Andrew, he came from Bethsaida.
Clue 8: He brought his friend Nathanael to meet Jesus.
Clue 9: He told Nathanael, "Come and see."
Clue 10: He was one of the Twelve Apostles, and his name means "lover of horses."

Clue 1: In Michelangelo's Last Judgment in the Sistine Chapel, this saint holds his own skin.
Clue 2: Tradition says he was skinned alive in Armenia.
Clue 3: He is a patron saint of tanners and leatherworkers.
Clue 4: His feast day is August 24.
Clue 5: Tradition says he preached in India and Armenia.
Clue 6: He came from Cana in Galilee.
Clue 7: He asked, "Can anything good come from Nazareth?"
Clue 8: Jesus said he was an Israelite with no deceit in him.
Clue 9: Jesus saw him sitting under a fig tree before Philip called him.
Clue 10: He was one of the Twelve Apostles and is also called Nathanael.

Clue 1: According to tradition, this saint was killed with a spear near present-day Chennai, India.
Clue 2: An ancient community of Christians in Kerala, India, is named after him.
Clue 3: He is the patron saint of architects and builders.
Clue 4: He was also called "Didymus," which means "the Twin."
Clue 5: When Jesus went back toward Judea, he said, "Let us also go, that we may die with Him."
Clue 6: He asked Jesus, "Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?"
Clue 7: He was not with the other Apostles when the risen Jesus first appeared to them.
Clue 8: He said he would not believe unless he put his finger into Jesus' wounds.
Clue 9: When he saw the risen Jesus, he cried out, "My Lord and my God!"
Clue 10: He is often called the "doubting" Apostle.

Clue 1: According to legend, this saint was martyred in Ethiopia.
Clue 2: Caravaggio painted three famous pictures of him for a chapel in Rome.
Clue 3: His symbol is a winged man.
Clue 4: His Gospel begins with the family tree of Jesus.
Clue 5: His Gospel tells the story of the Magi visiting the Christ Child.
Clue 6: He threw a big dinner for Jesus that many sinners attended.
Clue 7: He was also called Levi.
Clue 8: Jesus called him from his customs post, saying, "Follow me."
Clue 9: He wrote the first Gospel in the New Testament.
Clue 10: He was a tax collector before becoming an Apostle.

Clue 1: In art, this saint often wears a medallion with the face of Jesus, linked to a legend about King Abgar of Edessa.
Clue 2: He is often shown with a flame above his head, recalling Pentecost.
Clue 3: He shares his feast day, October 28, with St. Simon.
Clue 4: Tradition says he and St. Simon were martyred together in Persia.
Clue 5: At the Last Supper he asked Jesus why He would show Himself to the disciples and not to the world.
Clue 6: A one-chapter letter near the end of the New Testament is traditionally credited to him.
Clue 7: Entertainer Danny Thomas founded a famous children's hospital in Memphis in his honor.
Clue 8: Some people once avoided praying to him because his name sounded like the name of the traitor.
Clue 9: He was one of the Twelve Apostles and is also called Thaddeus.
Clue 10: He is the patron saint of hopeless causes.

Clue 1: According to one legend, this Apostle was martyred by being sawn in half.
Clue 2: Because of this, he is often shown in art holding a saw.
Clue 3: He is a patron saint of woodcutters and tanners.
Clue 4: Some traditions say he preached in Egypt.
Clue 5: He shares his feast day, October 28, with St. Jude.
Clue 6: Tradition says he was martyred in Persia along with St. Jude.
Clue 7: Some Gospels call him "the Cananaean."
Clue 8: The Gospels say almost nothing about him except his name.
Clue 9: His nickname suggests he once belonged to a group eager to drive out the Romans.
Clue 10: He was one of the Twelve Apostles, called "the Zealot" to tell him apart from Simon Peter.

Clue 1: This saint's relics are said to rest in Trier, making him the only Apostle believed buried in Germany.
Clue 2: He was chosen over a man named Joseph Barsabbas, also called Justus.
Clue 3: His feast day is May 14.
Clue 4: In art he is often shown holding an axe.
Clue 5: He had followed Jesus from His baptism by John until the Ascension.
Clue 6: He was chosen by casting lots.
Clue 7: He was chosen in Jerusalem shortly before Pentecost.
Clue 8: St. Peter led the meeting at which he was chosen.
Clue 9: He was not one of the original Twelve called by Jesus.
Clue 10: He was chosen to replace Judas among the Twelve Apostles.

Clue 1: Ancient tradition says this saint painted the first icon of the Virgin Mary.
Clue 2: He is a patron saint of artists and painters.
Clue 3: He was a Gentile, possibly the only non-Jewish writer of the New Testament.
Clue 4: His symbol is a winged ox.
Clue 5: He traveled with St. Paul and sometimes writes "we" in telling the story.
Clue 6: He also wrote the Acts of the Apostles.
Clue 7: Only his Gospel tells of the shepherds visiting the newborn Jesus in the manger.
Clue 8: His Gospel includes the parables of the Prodigal Son and the Good Samaritan.
Clue 9: St. Paul called him "the beloved physician."
Clue 10: He was a doctor and wrote the third Gospel.

Clue 1: Before his conversion, this saint was a Roman general named Placidus.
Clue 2: He served under the Emperor Trajan.
Clue 3: His wife and two sons were baptized with him.
Clue 4: Legend says his family was separated by misfortune and later reunited.
Clue 5: Legend says he and his family were martyred inside a bronze bull heated by fire.
Clue 6: A church near the Pantheon in Rome is named for him, and its roof has a stag's head with a cross.
Clue 7: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 8: He is a patron saint of hunters.
Clue 9: While hunting, he saw a crucifix between the antlers of a stag.
Clue 10: He was a Roman general converted by a vision of a stag.

Clue 1: This saint is the first known writer to use the phrase "the Catholic Church."
Clue 2: Tradition says he was the child Jesus placed in the middle of the disciples.
Clue 3: He called himself "Theophorus," meaning "God-bearer."
Clue 4: He wrote seven letters to churches while being taken to Rome as a prisoner.
Clue 5: He begged the Christians of Rome not to try to save him from death.
Clue 6: He wrote, "I am the wheat of God, ground by the teeth of wild beasts."
Clue 7: He was the third bishop of the city where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.
Clue 8: He is said to have been a disciple of St. John the Apostle.
Clue 9: He was thrown to the lions in Rome.
Clue 10: He was a bishop of Antioch and an early martyr.

Clue 1: When this saint was burned at the stake, witnesses said the flames formed an arch around him and did not burn him.
Clue 2: He was then killed with a dagger, and so much blood flowed that it put out the fire.
Clue 3: Told to curse Christ, he said, "Eighty-six years I have served Him, and He has done me no wrong."
Clue 4: His name means "much fruit" in Greek.
Clue 5: He traveled to Rome to discuss the date of Easter with Pope Anicetus.
Clue 6: He received a letter from St. Ignatius of Antioch.
Clue 7: St. Irenaeus heard him preach as a boy.
Clue 8: The account of his death is one of the oldest martyr stories outside the Bible.
Clue 9: He was the bishop of Smyrna, in modern Turkey.
Clue 10: He was a disciple of St. John the Apostle who died a martyr in old age.

Clue 1: This saint wrote a long dialogue with a Jewish man named Trypho.
Clue 2: He was born in Flavia Neapolis in Samaria.
Clue 3: He studied Stoic, Pythagorean, and Platonic philosophy before becoming a Christian.
Clue 4: An old man he met by the sea led him to Christ.
Clue 5: He kept wearing a philosopher's cloak after his conversion.
Clue 6: He wrote one of the earliest descriptions of the Mass.
Clue 7: He wrote "Apologies" defending Christianity to the Roman emperor.
Clue 8: He is the patron saint of philosophers.
Clue 9: He was beheaded in Rome around 165 AD.
Clue 10: He was a great early defender of the faith whose name includes the title "Martyr."

Clue 1: In 2022, Pope Francis declared this saint a Doctor of the Church with the title "Doctor of Unity."
Clue 2: He wrote a five-book work called "Against Heresies."
Clue 3: He fought against the Gnostic heresy.
Clue 4: He listed the bishops of Rome from St. Peter down to his own time.
Clue 5: He was one of the first to insist that there are exactly four Gospels.
Clue 6: He wrote, "The glory of God is man fully alive."
Clue 7: As a boy he listened to St. Polycarp preach.
Clue 8: He came from Smyrna in Asia Minor.
Clue 9: He became bishop of a city in Gaul after its bishop was martyred.
Clue 10: He was the bishop of Lyon, France, and is a Church Father.

Clue 1: When this saint's tomb was opened in 1599, the sculptor Stefano Maderno carved her body as it was found.
Clue 2: She was a Roman noblewoman who had promised her virginity to God.
Clue 3: On her wedding night she told her husband Valerian that an angel guarded her.
Clue 4: Her husband and his brother Tiburtius both became Christians and martyrs.
Clue 5: Her executioner struck her neck three times but could not cut off her head.
Clue 6: She lived for three days after the attempt to behead her.
Clue 7: She is one of the women named in the Roman Canon of the Mass.
Clue 8: Her feast day is November 22.
Clue 9: Legend says she sang to God in her heart while the music played at her wedding.
Clue 10: She is the patron saint of music and musicians.

Clue 1: This saint was sent from Rome to Gaul along with his companions Rusticus and Eleutherius.
Clue 2: He was martyred on a hill in Paris now called Montmartre, the "Mount of Martyrs."
Clue 3: Legend says that after he was beheaded, he picked up his head and walked several miles, preaching.
Clue 4: The basilica named after him became the burial place of the kings of France.
Clue 5: In art he is often shown holding his own head.
Clue 6: He is invoked against headaches.
Clue 7: His feast day is October 9.
Clue 8: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 9: He is a patron saint of France.
Clue 10: He was the first bishop of Paris.

Clue 1: Legend says this saint was a giant named Reprobus who wanted to serve the most powerful king in the world.
Clue 2: He left a king who feared the devil, then left the devil because the devil feared the cross.
Clue 3: A hermit told him to serve Christ by carrying people across a dangerous river.
Clue 4: Legend says his staff blossomed after he planted it in the ground.
Clue 5: In 1969 his feast was removed from the universal calendar, but he is still a saint.
Clue 6: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 7: Many people keep his medal in their cars.
Clue 8: His name means "Christ-bearer."
Clue 9: He carried a child across a river who grew heavier and heavier and turned out to be Christ.
Clue 10: He is the patron saint of travelers.

Clue 1: Some of this saint's relics are kept at Whitefriar Street Church in Dublin, Ireland.
Clue 2: He was a priest martyred in Rome around 269 AD under Emperor Claudius II.
Clue 3: He was buried along the Via Flaminia, north of Rome.
Clue 4: Legend says he healed the blind daughter of his jailer.
Clue 5: Legend says he wrote a farewell letter to the jailer's daughter before his execution.
Clue 6: Legend says he secretly married couples when the emperor forbade soldiers to marry.
Clue 7: The poet Geoffrey Chaucer is the first writer known to link his day with romantic love.
Clue 8: He is the patron saint of engaged couples and love.
Clue 9: His feast day is February 14.
Clue 10: People send cards, flowers, and chocolates on his feast day.

Clue 1: After this saint survived his first execution, a widow named Irene nursed him back to health.
Clue 2: He was buried in the catacombs on the Appian Way, where a basilica now bears his name.
Clue 3: He was a captain in the Praetorian Guard under Emperor Diocletian.
Clue 4: As a soldier, he secretly encouraged Christians who were in prison.
Clue 5: After recovering, he confronted the emperor and was clubbed to death.
Clue 6: His feast day is January 20.
Clue 7: He is invoked against the plague.
Clue 8: He is a patron saint of athletes and soldiers.
Clue 9: He was tied to a post and shot with arrows.
Clue 10: He is the Roman soldier martyr almost always painted pierced with arrows.

Clue 1: In 1087, Italian sailors carried this saint's relics from Asia Minor to Bari, Italy.
Clue 2: A sweet-smelling liquid called "manna" is said to flow from his relics.
Clue 3: Legend says he slapped the heretic Arius at the Council of Nicaea.
Clue 4: Legend says he brought back to life three boys who had been killed by a butcher.
Clue 5: He is a patron saint of sailors.
Clue 6: He is a patron saint of children.
Clue 7: His feast day is December 6.
Clue 8: He secretly tossed bags of gold through a window so three poor sisters could marry.
Clue 9: He was the bishop of Myra, in modern Turkey.
Clue 10: He is the original "Santa Claus."

Clue 1: Legend says a wolf returned a poor woman's pig at this saint's command.
Clue 2: He was the bishop of Sebaste in Armenia.
Clue 3: Legend says that while he hid in a cave, wild animals came to him for healing.
Clue 4: In prison, the woman whose pig was returned brought him food and candles.
Clue 5: He was tortured with iron combs used for carding wool and then beheaded.
Clue 6: He is the patron saint of wool combers.
Clue 7: His feast day is February 3, the day after Candlemas.
Clue 8: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 9: He saved a boy who was choking on a fishbone.
Clue 10: On his feast day, throats are blessed with two crossed candles.

Clue 1: Legend says this saint had a third window added to her father's bathhouse in honor of the Trinity.
Clue 2: Her pagan father Dioscorus locked her in a tower.
Clue 3: In art she is usually shown with a tower that has three windows.
Clue 4: Her own father beheaded her, and then he was struck by lightning.
Clue 5: She is a patron saint of artillerymen and miners.
Clue 6: She is a patron saint of people who work with explosives.
Clue 7: On her feast day, December 4, people cut cherry branches hoping they will bloom by Christmas.
Clue 8: She is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 9: A city on the California coast is named after her.
Clue 10: She is invoked against lightning and sudden death.

Clue 1: This saint is the patron of Squillace, a town in Calabria, Italy, which claims his relics.
Clue 2: His name comes from a Greek word meaning "innocent" or "without evil."
Clue 3: Emperor Constantine is said to have built a church in his honor in Constantinople.
Clue 4: He came from Cappadocia, in modern Turkey.
Clue 5: He openly declared his faith and refused to sacrifice to the pagan gods.
Clue 6: He was tortured and then beheaded.
Clue 7: He was martyred at Byzantium around 303 AD, under Emperor Diocletian.
Clue 8: He is invoked against headaches.
Clue 9: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 10: He was a Roman centurion martyr known by two names, one of them Acacius.

Clue 1: Legend says this saint freed Emperor Diocletian's daughter Artemia from an evil spirit.
Clue 2: Legend says he then traveled to Persia and freed the Persian king's daughter as well.
Clue 3: He was a deacon in Rome under Pope Marcellus.
Clue 4: He was forced to do hard labor building the Baths of Diocletian.
Clue 5: He helped feed and care for other Christian prisoners.
Clue 6: He was martyred on the Via Salaria with his companions Largus and Smaragdus.
Clue 7: His feast day is August 8.
Clue 8: He is invoked against evil spirits and temptation at the hour of death.
Clue 9: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 10: He was a Roman deacon and martyr famous for casting out demons.

Clue 1: This saint was bishop of Formia, Italy, and his relics are in the cathedral of Gaeta.
Clue 2: Legend says he hid from persecution on Mount Lebanon, where a raven fed him.
Clue 3: In art he is often shown holding a windlass, a winch used on ships.
Clue 4: A gruesome later legend says his intestines were wound out on a windlass.
Clue 5: He is invoked against stomach pains.
Clue 6: His feast day is June 2.
Clue 7: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 8: The glowing light seen on ships' masts during storms is named after him.
Clue 9: He is the patron saint of sailors.
Clue 10: He is a bishop martyr also known by the name Elmo.

Clue 1: Tradition says this saint was born in Cappadocia and martyred at Lydda in Palestine.
Clue 2: Crusaders spread devotion to him throughout Europe.
Clue 3: He is a patron saint of Portugal and Catalonia.
Clue 4: He was a soldier in the Roman army who refused to persecute Christians.
Clue 5: His feast day is April 23.
Clue 6: He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
Clue 7: He is the patron saint of England, and his red cross is on its flag.
Clue 8: He is a patron saint of soldiers and Boy Scouts.
Clue 9: Legend says he rescued a princess from a monster.
Clue 10: He is the saint who slew the dragon.

Clue 1: In 836, this saint's relics were moved from Saint-Denis in France to Corvey Abbey in Germany.

Clue 1: This saint was exiled five times by four different Roman emperors.

Clue 1: This saint presided over the First Council of Constantinople in 381 for a time, then resigned.

Clue 1: This saint built a huge complex of hospitals and shelters for the poor near Caesarea, later named after him.

Clue 1: As a girl, this saint was nicknamed "wine-bibber" by a servant after secretly sipping wine.

Clue 1: This saint made Emperor Theodosius do public penance for a massacre before letting him back into church.

Clue 1: This saint was born in Stridon, in Dalmatia.

Clue 1: In 2004, Pope John Paul II returned some of this saint's relics from Rome to Constantinople.

Clue 1: As a teenager, this saint stole pears from a neighbor's tree just for the thrill of it.

Clue 1: As a girl, this saint ran away with her brother Rodrigo hoping to be martyred by the Moors.

Clue 3: Legend says that after falling in a river she told God, "If this is how you treat your friends, no wonder you have so few!"

Clue 5: She wrote "The Interior Castle."

Clue 1: In 1544, while this saint prayed in the catacombs, a ball of fire is said to have entered his mouth and enlarged his heart.

Clue 3: He started a pilgrimage walk to the Seven Churches of Rome.

Clue 5: Legend says he told a gossip to scatter a chicken's feathers and then gather them all back up.
Clue 6: He founded the Congregation of the Oratory.

Clue 8: He is called "the Apostle of Rome."
Clue 9: He loved jokes and was famous for his sense of humor.

Clue 1: This saint survived an assassination attempt when a bullet bounced off him while he prayed.

Clue 1: As a child, this saint was saved from drowning in a well by a lady he believed was the Virgin Mary.

Clue 1: This saint slipped pamphlets under doors to reach Calvinists in the Chablais region.

Clue 1: This saint was the son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed slave from Panama.

Clue 1: This saint said he was captured by pirates and sold as a slave in Tunis.

Clue 1: This saint lived alone in a tiny hut she built in her family's garden.

Clue 1: This saint's confessor was St. Claude de la Colombière.

Clue 1: After losing a court case in Naples, this saint gave up law and said, "World, I know you now."

Clue 1: In 1809 this saint was drafted into Napoleon's army but ended up hiding as a deserter.

Clue 1: At age nine, this saint dreamed that a pack of wild animals turned into gentle lambs.

Clue 1: This saint's family lived in a former jail cell called "le cachot."

Clue 1: When this young heiress asked Pope Leo XIII for missionaries, he suggested she become a missionary herself.
